rules.description: Every call returns well-formed actions on known requests (book only a waiting request, move or release only an upcoming appointment) with a date inside the booking window (the next 10 working days); a call that fails or times out breaks it too.
A doctor's 20-minute slot holds at most one appointment.
An appointment uses the calendar's session slots of its doctor and day; a new-patient visit takes two consecutive slots of the same session, a follow-up one.
A request is booked with a doctor of its department.
The Dermatology clinic is closed on City Day, Monday 23 November 2026, although the calendar still lists its sessions; no Dermatology appointment that day.
No appointment before the request's earliest date.

At most 4 new-patient visits per day hospital-wide with a doctor who does not speak the patient's language (each needs one of the in-person interpreters; medium+, one fewer on the day an interpreter is away).
The lab takes at most 7 fasting blood tests per working day.
A request that needs the fasting blood test has its test day from its earliest date to the working day before the visit (a newly set test day in the future).
Once an absence notice has arrived, no appointment stays or is booked with that doctor on a day of the absence.
Every urgent (U) request is booked the day it arrives, within 2 working days of its first possible day (earliest date or the next working day), and stays within that window.

The first three slots of every morning session (09:00, 09:20 and 09:40) are held for urgent requests until the working day before; no S or R request is booked or moved into them two or more working days ahead.

When the hospital changes the day or time of a patient's appointment, the new appointment is at least 3 working days after the day of the change; for a request the hospital released and books again later, after the day of the release (another doctor at the same day and time needs no notice).

Waiting requests are booked in the priority order (urgent (U) requests first, then everyone else (S and R together) strictly by the date received, first come first served); a request is not booked while a request of higher priority of the same department, visit type and previous doctor still waits and could have taken that slot.
A follow-up is booked with the patient's previous doctor; a habit the head of the outpatient office can grant exceptions to.
